_doc_walkSceneKey: the town's EXPLORABLE scene key — stated role, not inferred (district fixed-camera bundles carry the whole town's collision, so pad names cannot identify the walk scene). This is the real-time DEVELOPER view; the game routes players into playSceneKey. Built by tools/emb_blockout.py, exported by tools/emb_export.py.
_doc_playSceneKey: the scene the GAME sends players to — the town played as a sequence of FIXED pre-rendered shots (the FF grammar this project exists for). Deliberately separate from walkSceneKey: the real-time bundle stays the developer's explore view, and which of the two the scene graph wires is a data choice, not a naming coincidence.
_doc_cameraFile: the hand-authored camera INTENT for playSceneKey. tools/cine_solve.mjs --town emberbrook solves it against this map + the emb-walk walk geometry into emberbrook.cameras.solved.json — the one numeric truth cine_bake.py and play3d.html both read.
premise: The home village: a valley farming settlement gathered around its living Heartlight — one of the last — where the village brook meets the river. Warm, low, earthbound; everything Dellhollow is not. The river is the story's spine: Vesper arrives along it, and leaves through the Sigil Gate to follow it downstream.
units: world units (1u ~ 1m). Axes: x = west-east, y = south-north, z = height (village sits on a gentle rise, z 0..3).

river._doc: USER CANON 2026-07-31: Vesper has been following the river; her maps say continue downstream. The river leads through Emberbrook and beyond the old (Sigil) gate — which is why she must pass through — and onward to Dellhollow, where the journey continues along the same water. Build: visible vista east of town, NOT walkable.
river.flow: south-to-north (downstream; Dellhollow lies downstream beyond the Sigil Gate)

brook._doc: USER REDLINE 2026-07-31: Emberbrook gets its brook. Springs under the hilltop, runs down between Home Row and the square, feeds the pond, and slips into the river at a confluence east of the pond. One plank footbridge on Pond Lane.

lamps._doc: STORY.md §2 CANON, build guidance: a lamppost near every home; Lake's dusk rounds run in fixed order — low ground first (POND LANE, where moths rise off the water at dusk), then inward, ENDING at the lamps nearest the Heartlight: 'closing the ring' before full dark. Lamp placement + route must stage this. NOTE: Lake carries the brass LIGHTER (a seed-ember) on the rounds — the Heartlight itself never leaves its pedestal.

impliedScale._doc: USER RULING 2026-07-31: Emberbrook must READ as a lovely, lively town with deep history and a vibrant community — that is what a Heartlight DOES for a town — while chapter one stays focused and tight. Build the town to HINT at being much larger than the playable area: the player does not (and should not) have access to the whole town. Techniques, in canon order of preference: (1) non-walkable massing beyond every playable edge — further rooftops, chimney smoke, lit windows, hillside cottages, always composed into the camera frames; (2) lanes that visibly CONTINUE but are closed at the threshold (festival carts, stacked barrels, a hedge stile — soft, believable closures, never invisible walls); (3) at the Kindling Hour the square is CROWDED with background villagers — non-interactable or barely so; named cast are the interactive minority. The walk network stays exactly as tight as the parcels; the LOOK says big, the WALK says chapter one.
